info.title: How Upcheck Works
info.subtitle: Data sources, vulnerability detection, and categorization
info.sources_title: How We Fetch Latest Versions & Announcements
info.npm_registry_desc: Queries registry.npmjs.org directly to fetch the latest published version, release dates, and repository links.
info.deprecation_desc: When a package author or maintainer deprecates a package (e.g. request, moment), they publish an official announcement reason to NPM. Upcheck extracts this string and surfaces it prominently.
info.osv_desc: Upcheck queries OSV for the analyzed direct dependency versions and fetches advisory details. Unknown severities are marked explicitly; this does not replace a lockfile audit.
info.cat_critical_desc: Known high or critical severity CVE/GHSA (CVSS ≥ 7.0). Requires immediate update or patching.
info.cat_security_desc: Moderate or low severity advisory present in database. Review and apply security fixes.
info.cat_deprecated_desc: Maintainer or author announced end-of-life or recommended replacement package.
info.cat_major_desc: Semver major jump (e.g. v15 to v16). Review release notes for API, config, and runtime changes before updating.
info.cat_minor_desc: Backwards-compatible feature additions and performance improvements.
info.cat_patch_desc: Backwards-compatible bug fixes and stability tweaks. Very safe to upgrade.
info.cat_up_to_date_desc: Matches current latest stable release in npm registry with 0 known vulnerabilities.

cookie.message: Upcheck does not use advertising or analytics cookies. It stores your scan history and cache only in this browser; an optional GitHub token stays in memory for the current session.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How Upcheck processes repository manifests, browser storage and optional GitHub tokens.
privacy.processing_text: Upcheck receives the repository identifier or package.json content you submit in order to retrieve package metadata from GitHub and npm and check known vulnerabilities with OSV. It does not need your source code to perform an analysis.
privacy.storage_text: Your language preference, recent scan list and cached analysis results are stored in your browser’s local storage. They are not written to an Upcheck application database. You can remove them through your browser settings.
privacy.token_text: If you add a token, it remains only in the page’s memory and is cleared when you refresh or close it. The browser sends it only with the analysis request so Upcheck can call GitHub on your behalf. Use a read-only token with the smallest scope necessary and never share it on a shared device.
privacy.services_text: Analysis queries GitHub, the npm registry and the OSV vulnerability database. Those services process requests according to their own policies. Infrastructure providers may retain technical security logs as required to operate the service.
privacy.cookies_text: Upcheck does not use advertising or analytics cookies. The privacy notice dismissal and app preferences are stored locally in the browser.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: Terms governing use of the Upcheck dependency analysis service.
terms.purpose_text: Upcheck helps you inspect JavaScript dependency manifests for available releases, deprecations and known vulnerability records. It is an informational tool, not a guarantee that a project is secure or compatible after an update.
terms.responsibilities_text: Only submit repositories and manifests you are authorized to analyze. Review changelogs, lockfiles and test results before applying generated commands or recommendations. Keep any GitHub token confidential and use the minimum required scope.
terms.data_text: Results depend on GitHub, npm and OSV data, which may be incomplete, delayed or inaccurate. Upcheck is not responsible for changes to those services or for decisions made from their data.
terms.availability_text: The service may be changed, suspended or discontinued. Features are provided as available without a warranty of uninterrupted operation or fitness for a specific purpose.
